---
title: "Part 1 — Inside a Sandcastle"
---

Part 1 establishes what a **Sandcastle** is and what it isn't, and
walks through the five construction-layer concerns that make it
suitable for safely producing Open Engineering artifacts:

1. **Isolated workspaces** — the sandbox boundary.
2. **Repo/branch flow** — how work moves in and out durably.
3. **Tools and permissions** — what the engineering agent can and
   cannot do.
4. **Agent iteration** — the inner loop the agent runs inside the
   Sandcastle.
5. **Artifact boundaries** — what survives when the Sandcastle is
   torn down.

The single Part 1 lesson develops the mental model the rest of the
course will build on. It is intentionally instruction-first: the
runnable Sandcastle lab is planned for a later curriculum wave and is
clearly labelled in [Lesson 1's Lab page](01-inside-a-sandcastle/lab.qmd).

## Lessons

Lessons in Part 1 use the same lesson layout as the
[Pico Introduction lesson](../../pico/part-1/01-introduction/index.html)
and the [Crossplane Part 1 lesson](../../crossplane/part-1/01-composing-hello-pico-on-kubernetes/index.html).

- [1. Inside a Sandcastle](01-inside-a-sandcastle/index.qmd) —
  introduces the Sandcastle construction layer, its five concerns, and
  how it sits between the Crossplane composition layer and the Pico
  runtime layer.

## Where the runnable lab will live

Once a first runnable Sandcastle lab is authored, it will be published
as a reusable lab under the repository-root `labs/` directory (for
example, `labs/hello-world-pico-sandcastle/`) so it can be reused from
other courses. Until then, Lesson 1's [Lab page](01-inside-a-sandcastle/lab.qmd)
is a **structured paper walkthrough** rather than an executable lab —
it is deliberately labelled as *not yet runnable* so it is never
mistaken for a runnable-contract entry.
